frame_lock.unit: One dated state of 'who owns the number' — who counts the audience, sets the clearing price, or admits the buyer — at one layer of the US ad transaction.
frame_lock.denominator: Per layer of the transaction (counts / prices / concentrates / targets / admits / meters / bases / units / takes), NOT per calendar year and NOT per medium.
frame_lock.window: 1833 (penny Sun) / 1869-1875 (N.W. Ayer, disclosed price) through the 2026 corpus freeze.
frame_lock.population: L0 claims (e#-/mech- ids) in the frozen 'admarket' graph that survived sourcing and grading, cross-checked against verification/verdicts-*.json; rejected ids quarantined to DEAD.

form.downgrade_reason: YES to the first four gate questions but ABSENT on 5 (no single system-wide point of insight — reform is local per era) and 6 (no resolution — the count is still a hole, the take still contested, PMax adoption rising). There is a followable action line and a system subject, but no single transformation and no new stable state, so this is not a full Truby story arc. Both ABSENTs are load-bearing; all-slots-filled would be the fabrication signature.

protagonist.stated_purpose: An independent, disclosed, auditable number. Verbatim anchors: advertisers 'pay the lowest amount possible' (AdWords Select launch, 20 Feb 2002, mech-adwords-001, grade A); and a third-party audit — the ABC, the world's first circulation auditing organisation (1914, e1-measurement-002, grade B).
protagonist.revealed_function: The regime reliably converts the party being judged into the party that owns the number: across ~185 years the seller counts the audience, sets the clearing price, and admits the buyer, and every independent count/price/gate is a hard-won, temporary exception that reverts to seller ownership.
protagonist.gap: The founding disciplines promised an independent number; the record shows the independent number was the ~90-year anomaly (1914-~2004) and the default is that the judged party owns it.
regimes_evidenced: Regime A — pre-1914 publisher self-counting (the default): the seller states its own circulation [e1-measurement-002 corrects era-1 self-counting].
Regime B — 2002+ platform self-count (the reversion): the seller records the impression, runs the auction, validates the click, bills its own log [e6-measurement-006, e6-measurement-001].
Regime C — the 1914-2004 reform interlude and the 1946 vendor transfer, showing the anomaly and its decay [e1-measurement-002, e2-measurement-003].
outcomes_unexplained: 1987 people meter: the honest count HURT the seller (CBS/ABC -13%). A 'seller inflates its own count' function does not predict a seller adopting an instrument that cut its own numbers [e4-measurement-001].
2021 MRC stripped Nielsen's accreditation — the surviving auditor bit the incumbent [e7-measurement-002].
The syndicated take-rate ratchet REVERSED under competition, 24.7%->21.3% (2006-08); a pure maximizer would not let the rate fall [mech-tac-003].

Bok 1892: Ladies' Home Journal refused patent-medicine revenue — a 'maximise advertiser payment' function does not predict a seller destroying its own inventory [tu:era:1:event:4, event node, no L0 number].
Direct-mail exclusion cuts both ways — over-booked as national in the Coen era, excluded in 2025; not a consistent 'seller inflates' direction [e7-scale-006].

designing_principle.statement: Re-enter the single question — who owns the number? — at each layer of the ad transaction in rough chronological order, and let the recurring answer (the judged party, by default) and its documented exceptions carry the argument. Never narrate a medium's 'conquest' or a platform's 'intent'.
claims_excluded: e2-creators-001 (JWT's 'nine weekly network shows') — REJECTED at the dataset layer; agency-craft color, not about who owns the number.
e7-medium-003 (mobile 66% of US digital 2025) — REJECTED; a medium-share statistic the principle explicitly refuses.
ds-total-001 (a single Coen/McCann nominal total) — REJECTED; the principle treats the total as a basis, not a fact.
ds-gdp-001 (a superseded ad/GDP series) — REJECTED; superseded by e2-scale-004/005 and e7-scale-002, kept only as a guard.

spine.abt: The US ad market's founding disciplines promised an independent number — a disclosed price (Ayer 1875) and a third-party count (ABC 1914) — AND the buyer built its own independent meter (keyed coupon -> pay-per-action) to escape the seller's count, BUT the party being judged kept ending up owning the number at every layer, so the independent count/price/gate was the ~90-year anomaly, not the default, THEREFORE the platform era is a reversion to the pre-1914 condition at platform scale with no enforceable third-party backstop, not a new medium's conquest — and the state only ever relocates or ceilings the structure, it rarely breaks it.
spine.structure: McPhee SPIRAL over chronology — the same question (who owns the number?) re-entered at widening layers, 1833/1869->2026, reveals deepening toward the platform reversion.
spine.runner_up: braided / mosaic gathering across the twelve threads sharing the verb 'owns / counts / prices / bases the market'.
spine.runner_up_reason: Rejected as the primary because the argument is recurrence at deepening layers, not parallel independent nodes. The braid is the honest fallback if the spine proves too load-bearing for the grade-B/C evidence at the edges (the era-7 surrender, the buyer pools, the denominator wedge are all C).
spine.boredom_permitted: Inside a documentary digression a preceding exhibit has paid for (e.g. an FCC-audited table), for a length not exceeding that exhibit; nowhere in the spiral's re-entries themselves.

slots.name: opener_nut_graf
slots.warrant: Opens on the platform-era default and states the governing thesis: the seller reports a growth rate but never an absolute count, a number-shaped hole, set against the 1914 third-party audit and the flat commission rate. The 'anomaly' reading is architect synthesis, not a corpus statement.

slots.name: origin_disclosed_price
slots.warrant: Re-enters at the pricing layer: the disclosed 15% is the visible top plate of the agency's take, and the ad-funded below-cost model (penny Sun 1833) supplies 64.9% of newspaper income by 1914. The 1875 Ayer open contract has no primary artifact in the corpus (see gap s-AYER).

slots.name: origin_thirdparty_count
slots.warrant: Re-enters at the counting layer: the ABC (1914) established a third-party audit that itself corrected era-1 publisher self-counting. The independent count begins here as the ~90-year anomaly.

slots.name: reversion_count_to_vendor
slots.warrant: Tracks the first reversion: after the CAB wound up, Hooper's vendor ratings ran about 20% above on the same method, inflated toward the paying side. Sequence only; no documented mechanism for the residual.

slots.name: the_stack
slots.warrant: Re-enters at the take layer: the middleman's cut was a 3-4 hand stack (network retained 73%, agency 15% also covering program production, station rep 5-20%, a hidden 2%); only the smallest plate was ever public. Adjacency across plates on incompatible bases.

slots.name: commission_mythbuster
slots.warrant: The myth-buster: the census rate held near 14% to 1992 and 71% of big advertisers were still on commission in 1982; the mix collapse followed the 1991-94 unbundling, and the corpus edge marks search as a non-driver. Sequence with a negative-causal guard.

slots.name: instrument_not_audience
slots.warrant: The instrument, not the audience: people meters (Sept 1987) recorded about 10% fewer prime-time viewers with no viewer leaving the couch — a documented instrument change, not a change in the world. Residual: the honest count hurt the seller.

slots.name: buyer_meter
slots.warrant: Re-enters on the demand side: the direct-response buyer paid per keyed action from the 1900s and never accepted the seller's audience count; its pay-per-action model reached 57% of internet revenue by 2008. The most-wanted independent number arrived in the one medium where the seller counts the actions too.

slots.name: front_door_admission
slots.warrant: The front door: admission opened (heads democratised) while dollars did not — national share rose 61.4 to 66.3% (2002-07); the commission-free self-serve door existed by 1914; the state expelled two buyer classes (1906 patent medicine, 1971 cigarettes).

slots.name: the_dial
slots.warrant: The dial: targeting got about 279,000x finer by 1975 yet the ~2% yield never moved, so the buyer stopped choosing the target (PMax, grade-C endpoint). The march was to the countable unit, not the person; the query was identity-free; ATT (2021) marks the state re-separating.

slots.name: governed_price
slots.warrant: The governed price: 'pay the lowest amount possible' (2002) sat on a seller-run, seller-validated, seller-billed log with no independent audit 2002-08; rGSP (2019) raised top-slot CPC 5.91% and advertisers cannot opt out; three court-named knobs are 'intentional pricing'. Overture's founding auction was pure first-price. Residual: the take rate reversed under competition.

slots.name: state_moves_the_stack
slots.warrant: The state moves the top of the stack: the market builds concentration by capital (Overture led on revenue; a bigger cheque, not a better auction), and the state relocates (1943, 1984), ceilings (1954), or names it unlawful with remedy pending (2025). Remedy is not deconcentration on this record.

slots.name: unit_born_unaudited
slots.warrant: The mechanism: each new carrier ships a new priced unit no third party can yet count, so the seller counts it first; the century-spanning Coen series understates internet by half and goes blind at the 2008 seam. Shares moved glacially (TV passed newspapers only in 1992, about 1%); the relay-race reading is dead. Synthesis, adjacency-grade.

slots.name: denominator_war
slots.warrant: The denominator war: direct mail was the largest-or-#2 medium for about 70 years yet is written out of the total 8 times and out of the 2025 basis entirely, so every 'share of advertising' is a claim about a basis. 1922 at 3.0% of GDP vs 2025 at ~1.32% is non-commensurable, the caveat non-removable. Dual-profile on one denominator.

slots.name: closer_reversion
slots.warrant: Closer: the platform era returns the pre-1914 condition at scale with no enforceable backstop; the count is still a hole (IAB scores >$26B misallocated); the AI box may transfer the funding click, a contested cross-section Google disputes. Returns to the opener's number-shaped hole.

slots.name: point_of_insight
slots.warrant: No single system-wide self-revelation. Reform is local per era (government 1912, MRC 1964); no dated moment shows the whole regime seeing itself differently. Confirmed independently by all six S2 digs. The absence is stated in the body.

slots.name: resolution_new_equilibrium
slots.warrant: No resolution. The situation is ongoing; the 'reversion' is a state, not a new stable end. The nearest steady state (reversion to pre-1914 at scale, no backstop) is explicitly not a resolution and is written as such.

slots.name: opponent_as_party
slots.warrant: No party villain. System subject: the slot is redesigned to a constraint — the economics of counting (whoever funds the count controls it). The strongest agency reading (platforms engineered it) is considered and not adopted; two intentional beats are surfaced, not adjudicated.

slots.name: decisive_battle
slots.warrant: No single battle. The nearest thing (the 2024-25 DOJ rulings) was not treated as pivotal for the whole regime at the time and its remedy is pending; it is downgraded to the nearest-thing-to-a-turning-point, not a climax.

slots.name: ayer_1875_primary_artifact
slots.warrant: No primary artifact for the founding disclosed-price scene (open contract, ledger, or client letter). The absence is named in the body; the disclosed-price discipline is evidenced downstream via e4-pricing-001 and e2-creators-002. Routed to research.

slots.name: subsidy_break_measure
slots.warrant: No corpus measure of publisher revenue dependence on search referral. The strong 'the 130-year subsidy is being broken' reading cannot be grounded; the AI-box beat ships as CONTESTED color only. Routed to research.

scenes.tagged_line: Google reports paid clicks up ~18% YoY (Q4 2008) but never an absolute count, CPC, or query count — a number-shaped hole.
scenes.whose_desire: the reader, for a real audience/price number
scenes.opposition: the seller owns the log
scenes.plan: disclose a growth rate, not a count
scenes.twist: the market ends where it began, minus the backstop

scenes.tagged_line: Penny Sun (3 Sep 1833): ad-funded below-cost content, ~15k/day within 2 years; by 1914 ads supply 64.9% of newspaper income.
scenes.whose_desire: the publisher, for a below-cost mass audience
scenes.opposition: content costs more than its price
scenes.plan: let the advertiser pay the difference
scenes.twist: the outside payer now holds leverage

scenes.tagged_line: ABC founded 1914: the world's first third-party circulation audit, a merger of publisher-led and advertiser-led bodies, correcting era-1 self-counting.
scenes.whose_desire: the national advertiser, for an independent count
scenes.opposition: publishers state their own circulation
scenes.twist: the anomaly starts here

scenes.tagged_line: CAB winds up (1946); Hooper's vendor ratings run ~20% above on the same method, inflated toward the paying side.
scenes.whose_desire: the vendor, to sell a count to both sides
scenes.opposition: the buyer committee that funded CAB
scenes.plan: move the count to a private vendor
scenes.twist: same method, higher number

scenes.tagged_line: 1938, FCC-audited: NBC+CBS retain 73% ($32,046,218), pay 27% to 253 affiliates — the only plate anyone could publish a figure for.
scenes.whose_desire: each hand in the stack, for its cut
scenes.opposition: the other plates on incompatible bases
scenes.plan: keep the stack's depth off the rate card
scenes.twist: the public plate is the smallest

scenes.tagged_line: AT&T sells time on its 13-station toll network at $2,600/hr (~$750k/yr), 1925 — before RCA bought the business; the chain's origin.
scenes.whose_desire: AT&T, to sell airtime as a toll service
scenes.opposition: a market with no priced airtime yet
scenes.plan: meter time like a phone call
scenes.twist: the first middleman is the phone company

scenes.tagged_line: Consent decree 1 Feb 1956 ends 15% enforcement; yet 71% of big advertisers are still on commission in 1982; census rate ~14% to 1992.
scenes.whose_desire: the historian's legend, for a clean death date
scenes.opposition: the census, which shows the rate held
scenes.plan: date the death to the decree
scenes.twist: era 3 is the commission's peak, not its death

scenes.tagged_line: People meters (Sept 1987) show ~10% fewer prime-time viewers (CBS/ABC -13%, NBC -4%) — nothing about the audience changed, only the instrument.
scenes.whose_desire: the buyer, for a truer count
scenes.opposition: the seller, whose numbers the count cuts
scenes.endpoint: the count falls with no viewer leaving
scenes.twist: the honest count hurt the seller

scenes.tagged_line: Direct-response buyers pay per keyed action from the 1900s; pay-per-action reaches 57% of US internet revenue by 2008 (up from 51%).
scenes.whose_desire: the direct-response buyer, for a keyed number it owns
scenes.opposition: the seller's audience count
scenes.plan: pay per measured action, not per thousand
scenes.twist: it wins where the seller counts the actions too

scenes.tagged_line: Heads democratised, dollars did not: national share rose 61.4 to 66.3% (2002-07); cigarettes off-air 2 Jan 1971 ($225M/yr class expelled).
scenes.whose_desire: the small buyer, for an un-gated door
scenes.opposition: the recognised-agency gate and the state bouncer
scenes.twist: the open door is the one with no visible doorman

scenes.tagged_line: Overture, Q4 2001: 442M intent-matched clicks 'with no cookie and no profile' — the identity-free window.
scenes.whose_desire: the buyer, to be matched to intent
scenes.opposition: the cost of profiling
scenes.plan: target the words typed, not the person
scenes.twist: the identity-free query was itself the anomaly

scenes.tagged_line: By 1975 direct mail addresses 71.1M households one at a time, ~279,000x finer than a spot; 2-of-100 was a successful campaign.
scenes.whose_desire: the buyer, for a finer target
scenes.opposition: the 2% yield floor
scenes.twist: so the buyer stops choosing at all

scenes.tagged_line: AdWords Select (20 Feb 2002): 'pay the lowest amount possible'; rGSP (2019) raises top-slot CPC 5.91% and advertisers cannot opt out.
scenes.whose_desire: the market, for a neutral price
scenes.opposition: the seller's revenue targets
scenes.endpoint: the price is governed, not neutral
scenes.twist: the seller sets the clearing price

scenes.tagged_line: Mehta FOF names three knobs — squashing ('Butternut Squash'), format pricing, rGSP — 'intentional pricing'; 5%+ raises, 'the results have been largely consistent — it can.'
scenes.whose_desire: the seller, to hit quarterly targets
scenes.opposition: advertisers who cannot opt out
scenes.twist: the squashing exponent is still undisclosed

scenes.tagged_line: Noble buys NBC Blue for $8M (12 Oct 1943): 'antitrust, not technology, created the third network.'
scenes.whose_desire: the state, to deconcentrate the networks
scenes.opposition: RCA's two-network hold
scenes.twist: the market did not make it; a state order did

scenes.tagged_line: Mehta (5 Aug 2024): 89.2% search, $26.3B default share in 2021; Brinkema (17 Apr 2025) — remedy is not deconcentration on this record.
scenes.whose_desire: the state, to name the concentration unlawful
scenes.opposition: a court remedy that may not deconcentrate
scenes.twist: the fourth turn of the same wheel

scenes.tagged_line: Targeting bought, not built: Google/DoubleClick $3.1bn (13 Apr 2007), MSFT/aQuantive ~$6bn, Yahoo/Right Media $680M, WPP/24-7 $649M.
scenes.whose_desire: the seller, to own the targeting machinery
scenes.opposition: targeting built by independents
scenes.plan: acquire it rather than build it
scenes.endpoint: the dial becomes a seller-owned asset
scenes.twist: bought, not built

scenes.tagged_line: Coen's series understates internet by half ($10,529M vs $21,206M, 2007) and stops at 2007 — the instrument goes blind as the new unit is born.
scenes.whose_desire: the historian, for a century-spanning number
scenes.opposition: a new unit no third party can yet count
scenes.endpoint: the series goes blind at the seam
scenes.twist: the instrument enacts the gap it measures

scenes.tagged_line: Direct mail: 16.8% peak (1938) -> largest single line $60,225M (2007) -> excluded from the $398B MAGNA total (2025).
scenes.whose_desire: the compiler, for a clean total
scenes.opposition: a channel no compiler holds franchise over
scenes.endpoint: the biggest line falls out of the total
scenes.twist: the same convention makes it biggest or invisible

scenes.tagged_line: 1922 at 3.0% of GDP vs 2025 at ~1.32% vs 1944 at 1.2% floor — the two series are non-commensurable; the caveat is non-removable.
scenes.whose_desire: the reader, for one comparable intensity
scenes.opposition: two incompatible bases across the 2008 seam
scenes.twist: the trough is understated by the channel dropped

scenes.tagged_line: The number-shaped hole persists: IAB scores >$26B misallocated; the AI box may transfer the funding click (8% vs 15%, Google disputes the study).
scenes.whose_desire: the reader, for a resolution
scenes.opposition: an ongoing, unresolved regime
scenes.endpoint: the count is still a hole
scenes.twist: the model reappears inside the answer box

hypothesis_diff.before: Each new medium captured the market from the last, culminating in a novel platform crisis Google/Meta engineered to extract rents.
hypothesis_diff.after: The judged party owning the number is the default; the independent count/price/gate was the ~90-year anomaly (1914-~2004). The platform era is a reversion to the pre-1914 condition at scale with no enforceable backstop, not a new medium's conquest, driven by a structural birth-motor (every new unit born un-audited).
hypothesis_diff.what_changed: The frozen inventory put the seller owning the count before 1914 (self-counting) and again after 2002, with residuals (1987 people meter, 2021 MRC, take-rate reversal, Bok 1892) where the honest number hurt whoever paid for it, which the agentic hypothesis cannot accommodate. What did NOT change is worth suspecting: the dossiers already carried the anomaly reading, so this architecture inherits rather than discovers it; the residual list and the DEAD column are the guard against the tidy version.
